newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures stalled at lower levels.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures stalled at lower levels.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were stalled at the early lower levels at midday on Friday.
The March contract was trading 27 cents off at $22.80 at 1245 GMT having hit an intra-day low of $22.65 a barrel. February gas oil was trading $3.25 off at $215.50 a tonne.
"It's (March Brent) held support at $22.65/68 pretty well," said one trader. "I don't think we'll see it heading down much lower."
"We've had two days of downside action which has shaken all but the most hardy longs out of the market," he added. "This might have cleared the way for some upside movement."
Many traders were looking to NYMEX for direction with some predicting a bounce on the New York exchange.
"NYMEX hasn't moved down quite so much and I can't see it falling that much lower with cold weather forecast for the northeastern states over the weekend," said another trader.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said the coldest air mass of the winter season was due to hit the northeast United States late on Friday.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said on Thursday that the region would experience above average heating oil demand for at least the next two weeks.
